Subject: Monthly consumption window & approval matrix — NovaHealth discovery follow-up

Samira / team — thanks again for the 30-minute sync earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key notes from the call
- Estimated consumption profile (your guidance): ~0.8B — 2.0B tokens / month (spiky during peak hours).
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + search re-rank; average seq length ~700 tokens.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC/private-inference preferred; procurement will own vendor review.

Unit-economics & first-pass validation (ballpark)
- On-demand (no commit): $45 / 1M tokens
- Committed (12-month): pricing tiers we'll propose formally, e.g. 800M @ $30 /1M, 1.5B @ $27 /1M, 2.0B @ $25 /1M (examples; exact tiers negotiable)
- Example monthly spend (illustrative):
  - 0.8B @ $30/1M => $24,000 / month
  - 2.0B @ $25/1M => $50,000 / month

Procurement / legal signals you mentioned
- NovaHealth procurement threshold: PO + enterprise legal review for vendors when monthly spend > $50k (Samira to confirm).
- Need for SSO/SOC2 evidence and a short SOW for pilot.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm the 0.8B — 2.0B monthly band as representative of month-1 (pilot) to month-6 (scale)?
2) If the >$50k/month PO threshold is correct, would you prefer we surface both an on-demand rate and committed tiers so procurement can compare?
3) I'll send a brief pricing appendix + SOW template (attached) and an example cost table. If procurement wants an initial estimate they can include in the PO routing, we can produce that by EOD.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-deck-v2.pdf, sow-template.docx

Thanks — I can be flexible on cadence; if helpful we can book a 15-min pricing walkthrough with procurement next week.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Monthly consumption window & approval matrix — NovaHealth discovery follow-up

Jordan — thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Consumption band: yes, 0.8B — 2.0B tokens/month is a fair view for planning. Pilot expected around the low end (800M) and production could approach the high end within 3–6 months if performance holds.
- Procurement threshold: internal rule of thumb is any recurring commitment or expected spend > $50k / month requires vendor onboarding + PO + legal review. For lower spend we can use a standard card or small PO.
- Security: please include SOC2 type II attestation and a short note on network isolation options (VPC or private deployment).

Actions from our side: I'll introduce you to our procurement lead (cc'd) so they have the pricing deck + SOW. They typically want a clear committed vs on-demand comparison and an itemized monthly cost table for routing.

One question: are the committed tiers flexible on term length? We prefer 6–12 month commits, but procurement sometimes pushes for quarterly reviews.

Best,
Samira Khan
Director, AI Product — NovaHealth
samira.k@novahealth.com

Team — forwarding the thread and the pricing appendices. Ask: can we approve a one-time onboarding concession to help unblock procurement? Recommendation and rationale below.

Summary / recommendation
- Account: NovaHealth (DEAL-7831). Estimated band 0.8B — 2.0B tokens/month; procurement threshold at ~$50k / month.
- Recommendation: offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month-1 committed spend, capped at $5,000, to offset integration/validation costs and accelerate PO issuance. Retail impact: small NRR hit but short sales cycle benefit and higher likelihood of a 12-month commit.
- Commercial flexibility: allow both 6- and 12-month commit options; price ladder as in my previous email.

Requested approvals
1) Approve onboarding credit: 10% month-1 commit, cap $5k? (yes/no)
2) Approve margin levers to present: standard 12-month tiered discounts (as above) + a one-time professional services line item (we bill or include up to 8 hours free).

If you want I can draft the short approval note to attach to the SOW for procurement. I will only send the formal SOW and DocuSign after we have internal sign-off on the concession.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Vivek for a quick yes/no so I can move the procurement conversation forward.
